correction.title: Sea and aerial drones attack Russia's fleet in Sevastopol
correction.detail: On 29 October 2022 aerial drones and drone boats attacked the Black Sea Fleet in Sevastopol; the Russian-installed governor counted nine aerial drones and seven uncrewed surface vessels, and Russia blamed Ukraine. It showed that naval bases were vulnerable to low-cost drone boats and reset how navies and investors valued small uncrewed surface vessels.

note: The 9 + 7 count is a statement by the Russian-installed Sevastopol governor; GeoConfirmed estimated six to eight drone boats and at least three ships hit. In the part of the page read (first 100k characters) Russia blames Ukraine (and the UK) and no official Ukrainian claim is reported, so the title's attribution was neutralised.
